items.followUp: Describe sexual reproduction and give one example.

rubric.why: Award 1 mark for explaining that asexual reproduction involves one parent and no gametes or fertilization.
rubric.how: Look for one parent and the absence of gametes or fertilization.

rubric.why: Award 1 mark for a valid example of asexual reproduction.
rubric.how: Accept a correct example and the organism or group in which it occurs.

modelAnswer: Asexual reproduction is reproduction from a single parent without gametes or fertilization.
For example, Amoeba reproduces by binary fission.

items.followUp: State where intracellular and extracellular enzymes act.

rubric.why: Award 1 mark for identifying that intracellular enzymes act inside the cell in which they are produced.
rubric.how: Look for the term intracellular and its location inside the cell.

rubric.why: Award 1 mark for identifying that extracellular enzymes are released to act outside the cell in which they are produced.
rubric.how: Look for the term extracellular and its location outside the producing cell or their secretion.

modelAnswer: Intracellular enzymes act inside the cell in which they are produced.
Extracellular enzymes are secreted and act outside the cell in which they are produced.

rubric.why: Award 1 mark for describing cofactors as nonprotein components required for enzyme activity, often inorganic ions.
rubric.how: Look for the term cofactor and its nonprotein nature or identification as an inorganic ion.

rubric.why: Award 1 mark for describing coenzymes as organic molecules that assist enzymes, often derived from vitamins.
rubric.how: Look for the term coenzyme and its organic nature or a valid related feature.

modelAnswer: Cofactors are nonprotein substances required for enzyme activity; they may be inorganic ions.
Coenzymes are organic nonprotein molecules that assist enzymes and are often derived from vitamins.
